tracks.title: Hook
tracks.text: Government funding's getting to be to the point where it's almost non-existent, so we need to depend on our donors to help us stay in business, take care of our clients.

tracks.title: Question
tracks.text: can you just tell me your name, your title here at CASS, and a little bit about, you know, like who you are?

tracks.title: Who She Is
tracks.text: I am the CFO here at CASS.

tracks.title: Question
tracks.text: And what led you to nonprofit finance, and what has kept you passionate about this work?

tracks.title: Why Nonprofit
tracks.text: I had been working in construction for over 20 years, and I was really ready for something new. The passion came when I started working for a company that was mission-driven, more so than driven just to make a profit.

tracks.title: Question
tracks.text: And how has your experience at CASS influenced the way you think about the connection between financial strategy and changing lives?

tracks.title: Mindful
tracks.text: It's made me more aware of how money is spent, what are we spending it on, why are we spending it, and of course, how much we're spending. I know that on a nonprofit, especially in the sector that we're in with the homeless shelters, we need to be well-aware and be mindful of how we spend money, because it's limited.

tracks.title: Question
tracks.text: So when you think about the responsibility of managing donor dollars, what does that responsibility mean to you?

tracks.title: Report Back
tracks.text: I need to know where the money's being spent. I need to be able to report back to people where that money was spent, why it was spent there. I need to also be able to let people know where we need money, where we have shortfalls, so that way our development team can go out and hopefully raise those funds.

tracks.title: Question
tracks.text: So how do you approach making difficult financial decisions while keeping the mission and the people that CASS serves at the center of those conversations?

tracks.title: Clients First
tracks.text: It's easy, just, they come first. Financial decisions are based on when the client's needs versus really our employees' needs. Clients come first. We have to make sure they are taken care of. That's what our mission is, to take care of the homeless. So if we don't make sure, if we don't put them first in all aspects of the operations of a business, we're not gonna be able to meet our mission.

tracks.title: Question
tracks.text: how can you make a donor feel confident that their money is going to the right place?

tracks.title: Not Frivolously
tracks.text: I want them to know that their funds are being put to use to improve homelessness. It is helping, it is only being used for that. It's not being used frivolously. It's only being used to help our clients. I can't stress that enough.

tracks.title: Question
tracks.text: Maybe you could describe your job.

tracks.title: Fulfilling
tracks.text: It's fulfilling. I'm happy with what I do, why I do it, and it's just fulfilling. Makes me feel like, it makes me a better person.
